meta.title: Fast Matrix Multiplication · Strassen / AlphaTensor Frontier
meta.verdict: Open for integer and GF(2) rank certificates.

strategy_note.text: A scheme with s products proves rank ≤ s. Refuting Record s proves rank ≥ s + 1. Five active hunts span rectangular integer rank ([MM-rec-3x3x4], [MM-rec-3x4x5] — both matched by DeepMind AlphaEvolve arXiv:2506.13131 Table 3), binary 4×4 ([MM-rec-4x4-f2] AlphaTensor 47 over GF(2); AlphaEvolve reached 48 over ℂ), Laderman's 3×3×3 integer frontier ([MM-rec-3x3x3]), and pre-CSE unit-coeff addition minimization ([MM-rec-3x3x3-hw]). For AlphaTensor’s factor archives, each column gives one term; transpose the third factor from (column, row) to (row, column) for MatMul.Term.output. For concrete coefficient tables, unfold IsMatMulSchemeInt or IsMatMulSchemeF2 and use decide +kernel. https://github.com/google-deepmind/alphatensor/tree/1949163da3bef7e3eb268a3ac015fd1c2dbfc767/algorithms

lemmas.title: Strassen’s seven products over the integers
lemmas.paper_notes: Give the three coefficient vectors for each product in Strassen’s 2×2 scheme. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02165411

lemmas.title: Strassen’s seven products over GF(2)
lemmas.paper_notes: Reduce the seven products modulo two and verify all tensor coefficients using AND and XOR.

lemmas.title: Compose integer schemes by tensor product
lemmas.paper_notes: Pair each term of one scheme with each term of the other. Factor the coefficient sum over these pairs. Using two 2×2 schemes with seven products gives a 4×4 scheme with 49.

lemmas.title: 3×3 by 3×4 over the integers
lemmas.paper_notes: Smirnov gives a 29-product upper bound, matched by both AlphaTensor (standard-arithmetic archive, key 3,3,4) and Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve (arXiv:2506.13131, Table 3); beating 29 (≤ 28) remains an open frontier. Wang, Theorem 1, proves a GF(2) lower bound of 25, which carries to ℤ by mod-2 reduction. https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/3x3x4.html · https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07280

lemmas.title: 4×4 by 4×4 over GF(2)
lemmas.paper_notes: Two levels of Strassen give the 49-product launch ceiling. AlphaTensor gives 47 over GF(2) (while Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve, arXiv:2506.13131, broke Strassen's 49 over ℂ with 48 products, leaving ℤ open and GF(2) at 47). Bläser’s small-format bound for ⟨n,m,n⟩ is 2mn + 2n − m − 2 for m ≥ n ≥ 3, giving 34 at n = m = 4. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05172-4 · https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131 · https://doi.org/10.1016/S0885-064X(02)00007-9

lemmas.title: 3×4 by 4×5 over the integers
lemmas.paper_notes: AlphaTensor gives 47 products with integer coefficients (standard-arithmetic archive, key 3,4,5), also matched by Google DeepMind AlphaEvolve (arXiv:2506.13131, Table 3); beating 47 (≤ 46) remains open. Permute the tensor dimensions to ⟨3,5,4⟩: Bläser’s kl + lm + k − l + m − 3 bound at (k,l,m) = (3,5,4) gives 34. An integer decomposition is also a complex decomposition. https://fmm.univ-lille.fr/3x4x5.html · https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131 · https://doi.org/10.1007/s000370050028
lemmas.use_case: Rectangular block-recursive GEMM microkernel for transformer projection layers and dense BLAS routines.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 3×3 by 3×3 over the integers (Laderman 1976 Record = 23, LB = 19)
lemmas.use_case: Recursive 3×3 block GEMM over arbitrary rings (exact integer, finite-field, and floating-point BLAS); 22 products breaks a 50-year open record.
lemmas.paper_notes: Famous open problem since Laderman (1976): best known integer rank for 3×3×3 is 23 products, Bläser's lower bound is 19. Launch ceiling = 23; certify Laderman at 23 or make history at 22!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: Hardware-Friendly 3×3×3 Scheme (Rank ≤ 23, {-1,0,1} Coeffs, Minimum Additions)
lemmas.use_case: Directly governs the practical crossover size where fast block-recursive GEMM beats schoolbook in BLIS/OpenBLAS/CUTLASS while preserving FP16/BF16 numerical stability.
lemmas.paper_notes: Constrains all factors to unit coefficients {-1, 0, 1} at rank ≤ 23 and minimizes `schemeAdditions` — the direct PRE-CSE addition count (distinct from 2025–2026 post-CSE rank-23 3×3×3 minimization, which reaches 55 additions using common-subexpression elimination). Classic Laderman uses ~98 pre-CSE additions; sparse unit-coeff decompositions (Courtois–Bard–Hulme / Smirnov–Sedoglavic) reach ~68–75 pre-CSE additions!
